findings.body: The browser rejects an attachment that the server-side upload validator is configured to accept.
findings.failure_mode: Client-side validation returns false before the valid attachment can be uploaded.
findings.impact: The browser rejects an attachment that the server-side upload validator is configured to accept.
findings.root_cause: The patch replaces the type-specific site setting with one hard-coded limit shared by images and attachments.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Discourse.SiteSettings.max_attachment_size_kb when type is "attachment"; apply any larger source-image allowance only to image uploads.
findings.title: The fixed client limit rejects attachments permitted by site configuration
findings.trigger: An administrator configures max_attachment_size_kb above 10240 and a user selects an attachment between 10 MB and that configured limit.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 182 replaces dynamic `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with hardcoded `10 * 1024`. For attachments, this ignores max_attachment_size_kb. When admin sets max_attachment_size_kb > 10240, valid attachments between 10MB and configured limit are rejected client-side.

findings.body: The controller launches the same expensive external conversion command five times before rejecting the upload, enabling avoidable CPU amplification and increasing upload latency.
findings.failure_mode: A deterministic conversion failure is repeatedly re-executed with identical input.
findings.impact: The controller launches the same expensive external conversion command five times before rejecting the upload, enabling avoidable CPU amplification and increasing upload latency.
findings.root_cause: The loop ignores both OptimizedImage.downsize's boolean result and whether an iteration made progress.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the return value and stop retrying when conversion fails or when the file size does not decrease; return a conversion-specific upload error.
findings.title: Failed conversions are retried five times without checking the result
findings.trigger: A logged-in user uploads an oversized corrupt image, unsupported image, or animated GIF for which OptimizedImage.downsize returns false without reducing tempfile.size.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 65-68 show loop runs 5 times without checking downsize return value. If OptimizedImage.downsize returns false (conversion fails), loop continues retrying identical failing operation 5 times, wasting CPU.

findings.body: Ruby retains only the later method definition, so the existing five-argument call raises ArgumentError and emoji resizing jobs fail.
findings.failure_mode: Existing calls using the original signature dispatch to a method accepting at most four arguments and terminate before conversion.
findings.impact: Ruby retains only the later method definition, so the existing five-argument call raises ArgumentError and emoji resizing jobs fail.
findings.root_cause: The patch attempts to overload a Ruby method by arity, but the later class-method definition overwrites the earlier one.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one backward-compatible method that accepts width and height, and add a distinctly named percentage/dimension-string method or normalize both supported argument forms inside a single variadic implementation.
findings.title: The second downsize definition replaces the existing five-argument API
findings.trigger: Jobs::ResizeEmoji or any existing caller invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height, opts).
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby overwrites methods with same name - the 4-arg version at line 145 is replaced. Jobs::ResizeEmoji calls `downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 args, which now raises ArgumentError since only 4-arg version exists.

raw_findings.impact: The browser rejects an attachment that the server-side upload validator is configured to accept.

raw_findings.title: The fixed client limit rejects attachments permitted by site configuration
raw_findings.trigger: An administrator configures max_attachment_size_kb above 10240 and a user selects an attachment between 10 MB and that configured limit.

raw_findings.body: The client rejects an image that requires no downsizing and would be valid according to the server configuration.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Browser validation blocks a server-valid image and displays an incorrect maximum.
raw_findings.impact: The client rejects an image that requires no downsizing and would be valid according to the server configuration.
raw_findings.root_cause: A hard-coded ingress limit is used without accounting for installations whose configured target limit is already larger.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make the source-image cap configurable and ensure it is never lower than max_image_size_kb, rather than replacing the configured value with an unconditional 10 MB cap.
raw_findings.title: The fixed client cap overrides valid image-size configurations above 10 MB
raw_findings.trigger: SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb is configured above 10240 and a user selects an image whose size is between 10 MB and the configured maximum.

raw_findings.body: validateUploadedFiles now returns true instead of the asserted false value, so the test suite fails and the new large-image behavior has no replacement assertion.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Continuous integration reports a deterministic assertion failure and does not verify the intended new boundary.
raw_findings.impact: validateUploadedFiles now returns true instead of the asserted false value, so the test suite fails and the new large-image behavior has no replacement assertion.
raw_findings.root_cause: The validation contract was changed without updating or replacing the test that explicitly asserts the previous configured-limit behavior.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the test to assert the intended acceptance-and-downsizing boundary and add a case above the new source-image cap; retain separate assertions for configured attachment limits.
raw_findings.title: The existing upload-size JavaScript test now fails
raw_findings.trigger: The JavaScript test suite runs the existing "prevents files that are too big from being uploaded" test, which sets max_image_size_kb to 5 and supplies a 10 KB image.

raw_findings.body: The user is told the maximum is 10240 KB even though a request below that size was rejected, encouraging repeated failed uploads.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Error handling presents a false actionable limit after the request is rejected upstream.
raw_findings.impact: The user is told the maximum is 10240 KB even though a request below that size was rejected, encouraging repeated failed uploads.
raw_findings.root_cause: The error message assumes every source of HTTP 413 enforces the newly hard-coded client cap.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Expose and display an ingress-size setting that matches the deployed request-body limit, or fall back to the relevant configured upload limit instead of hard-coding 10 MB.
raw_findings.title: HTTP 413 errors report a maximum unrelated to the rejecting server
raw_findings.trigger: A proxy or application server returns 413 with a request-body limit other than 10 MB, such as the documented deployment limit matching a 3 MB max_image_size_kb setting.

raw_findings.body: FileHelper.download stops reading only after crossing the fixed threshold and returns the partial tempfile; the controller can validate and store that truncated image or attachment as though it were the complete remote file.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A nominally successful synchronous API upload stores incomplete remote content.
raw_findings.impact: FileHelper.download stops reading only after crossing the fixed threshold and returns the partial tempfile; the controller can validate and store that truncated image or attachment as though it were the complete remote file.
raw_findings.root_cause: The dynamic download allowance was replaced by a fixed byte cap even though FileHelper.download returns partially downloaded files on limit exhaustion.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Choose a source limit that respects the relevant type-specific setting, and make the downloader raise and discard the tempfile when the response exceeds that limit instead of returning partial content.
raw_findings.title: API URL uploads above 10 MB can be silently truncated
raw_findings.trigger: An API submits a URL for a file larger than 10 MB while the corresponding configured image or attachment maximum is above 10 MB.

raw_findings.body: Images larger than max_image_size_kb are rejected by the proxy before this controller executes, so the advertised automatic downsizing feature does not work on the documented deployment configuration.
raw_findings.evidence: # allow users to upload large images that will be automatically reduced to allowed size
raw_findings.failure_mode: Production requests receive HTTP 413 before application-level downsizing is reachable.
raw_findings.impact: Images larger than max_image_size_kb are rejected by the proxy before this controller executes, so the advertised automatic downsizing feature does not work on the documented deployment configuration.
raw_findings.root_cause: The implementation separates the accepted source size from max_image_size_kb without updating the deployment contract that tells operators to use max_image_size_kb as the upstream request limit.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Introduce and document a separate maximum source-upload size, configure or instruct proxies to permit that value, and retain max_image_size_kb as the post-downsize target.
raw_findings.title: Documented reverse-proxy limits prevent the downsizing path from running
raw_findings.trigger: An installation follows the existing max_image_size_kb documentation and configures nginx, Apache, or another proxy to reject request bodies above that target size.

raw_findings.body: The animated implementation forwards "80%" to gifsicle's --resize-fit option, which expects width-by-height dimensions; conversion fails and the oversized GIF is ultimately rejected instead of downsized.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Every downsizing attempt exits unsuccessfully for the animated execution path.
raw_findings.impact: The animated implementation forwards "80%" to gifsicle's --resize-fit option, which expects width-by-height dimensions; conversion fails and the oversized GIF is ultimately rejected instead of downsized.
raw_findings.root_cause: A percentage expression supported by ImageMagick's resize syntax is passed through the shared API to a gifsicle command with a different dimension grammar.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Read the GIF dimensions and pass a concrete WxH target to the animated path, or implement percentage scaling with gifsicle's scaling option while preserving the existing dimension-based API.
raw_findings.title: Animated GIF downsizing passes an unsupported percentage to gifsicle
raw_findings.trigger: An oversized GIF is uploaded with allow_animated_thumbnails enabled and the tempfile path retains its .gif extension.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Introduce and document a separate maximum source-upload size, configure or instruct proxies to permit that value, and retain max_image_size_kb as the post-downsize target.
validated_findings.title: Documented reverse-proxy limits prevent the downsizing path from running
validated_findings.trigger: An installation follows the existing max_image_size_kb documentation and configures nginx, Apache, or another proxy to reject request bodies above that target size.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Claim about proxy rejecting before downsizing is speculative about deployment configuration. The patch doesn't change proxy behavior - it changes application code. Whether proxies are configured to match max_image_size_kb is external to this patch.

validated_findings.body: The animated implementation forwards "80%" to gifsicle's --resize-fit option, which expects width-by-height dimensions; conversion fails and the oversized GIF is ultimately rejected instead of downsized.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Every downsizing attempt exits unsuccessfully for the animated execution path.
validated_findings.impact: The animated implementation forwards "80%" to gifsicle's --resize-fit option, which expects width-by-height dimensions; conversion fails and the oversized GIF is ultimately rejected instead of downsized.
validated_findings.root_cause: A percentage expression supported by ImageMagick's resize syntax is passed through the shared API to a gifsicle command with a different dimension grammar.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Read the GIF dimensions and pass a concrete WxH target to the animated path, or implement percentage scaling with gifsicle's scaling option while preserving the existing dimension-based API.
validated_findings.title: Animated GIF downsizing passes an unsupported percentage to gifsicle
validated_findings.trigger: An oversized GIF is uploaded with allow_animated_thumbnails enabled and the tempfile path retains its .gif extension.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 67 passes '80%' to OptimizedImage.downsize. For animated GIFs, downsize_instructions_animated calls resize_instructions_animated which uses gifsicle with `--resize-fit #{dimensions}`. Gifsicle expects WxH format, not percentage. '80%' is invalid syntax for gifsicle --resize-fit.

validated_findings.body: The controller launches the same expensive external conversion command five times before rejecting the upload, enabling avoidable CPU amplification and increasing upload latency.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A deterministic conversion failure is repeatedly re-executed with identical input.
validated_findings.impact: The controller launches the same expensive external conversion command five times before rejecting the upload, enabling avoidable CPU amplification and increasing upload latency.
validated_findings.root_cause: The loop ignores both OptimizedImage.downsize's boolean result and whether an iteration made progress.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Capture the return value and stop retrying when conversion fails or when the file size does not decrease; return a conversion-specific upload error.
validated_findings.title: Failed conversions are retried five times without checking the result
validated_findings.trigger: A logged-in user uploads an oversized corrupt image, unsupported image, or animated GIF for which OptimizedImage.downsize returns false without reducing tempfile.size.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 65-68 show loop runs 5 times without checking downsize return value. If OptimizedImage.downsize returns false (conversion fails), loop continues retrying identical failing operation 5 times, wasting CPU.

validated_findings.body: The subsequent upload validator rejects the image even though the new client path admitted it with the promise that it would be reduced to the allowed size.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The downsizing loop exits with tempfile.size still above max_image_size_kb and upload creation returns a too-large error.
validated_findings.impact: The subsequent upload validator rejects the image even though the new client path admitted it with the promise that it would be reduced to the allowed size.
validated_findings.root_cause: The implementation uses an arbitrary fixed iteration count rather than a termination strategy tied to the configured target size.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Derive an initial dimension target from the required reduction, then continue only while conversions make progress until the size is valid or a documented minimum dimension/safety bound is reached.
validated_findings.title: Five 80% passes do not guarantee reaching the configured size
validated_findings.trigger: max_image_size_kb is configured substantially below the 10 MB source cap and an image remains above that target after five 80% dimension reductions.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: While mathematically true that 5 iterations of 80% may not reach target, this is a design limitation not a bug. The patch intentionally uses fixed iterations. Whether this is sufficient depends on input size ratios - not a clear defect.

validated_findings.body: Ruby retains only the later method definition, so the existing five-argument call raises ArgumentError and emoji resizing jobs fail.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Existing calls using the original signature dispatch to a method accepting at most four arguments and terminate before conversion.
validated_findings.impact: Ruby retains only the later method definition, so the existing five-argument call raises ArgumentError and emoji resizing jobs fail.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch attempts to overload a Ruby method by arity, but the later class-method definition overwrites the earlier one.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Keep one backward-compatible method that accepts width and height, and add a distinctly named percentage/dimension-string method or normalize both supported argument forms inside a single variadic implementation.
validated_findings.title: The second downsize definition replaces the existing five-argument API
validated_findings.trigger: Jobs::ResizeEmoji or any existing caller invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height, opts).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby overwrites methods with same name - the 4-arg version at line 145 is replaced. Jobs::ResizeEmoji calls `downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 args, which now raises ArgumentError since only 4-arg version exists.
